cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 118th Congress's districts (its file says session 118).
rec: 2022 congressional plan adopted by the Wisconsin Supreme Court: the Governor's plan (Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, 2022 WI 14, 'Johnson II')

Wisconsin Statutes ch. 3 (2021-22), note: the Act 44 plan is superseded by Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, 2022 WI 14, and the court-approved plan first applies to the 2022 general election

Chosen under the court's 'least change' approach after the Governor vetoed the Legislature's plan (Nov. 18, 2021). The U.S. Supreme Court (Mar. 23, 2022) vacated only the legislative part of Johnson II and left the congressional plan in place. Census check: cb_2022_us_cd118 (CDSESSN 118; lines supplied by the states by Aug. 31, 2022) holds this plan; 0 of 8 districts differ in shape from the 2024 file.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2022_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2022 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2022 legislative session year.
rec: 2022 legislative plan adopted by the Wisconsin Supreme Court: the Legislature's plan, 2021 Senate Bill 621 (Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, 2022 WI 19, 'Johnson III')

Wisconsin Statutes ch. 4 (2021-22), note: on April 15, 2022 the Wisconsin Supreme Court adopted 2021 Senate Bill 621 (Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, 2022 WI 19), which first applies to the 2022 general election

The court first adopted the Governor's legislative maps on Mar. 3, 2022; the U.S. Supreme Court reversed that on Mar. 23, 2022 (Wisconsin Legislature v. WEC), and on remand the court adopted S.B. 621, which the Governor had vetoed. Half the Senate (even-numbered districts) was elected in 2022. The Census file carries an extra 'ZZZ' record for area the state assigned to no district; it is not a district. Census check: cb_2022_us_sldu (LSY 2022, 34 districts; boundaries collected for the 2022 election year, file made April 2023); 31 of 34 districts differ in shape from the 2024 file.

Same plan and history as the Senate side: the Governor's maps (Mar. 3, 2022) were reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court and replaced by S.B. 621 on Apr. 15, 2022. The Census file carries an extra 'ZZZ' record for area the state assigned to no district; it is not a district. Census check: cb_2022_us_sldl (LSY 2022, 100 districts; boundaries collected for the 2022 election year, file made April 2023); 89 of 100 districts differ in shape from the 2024 file.
